messages.subject: Genotyping for a "four-way" cross
messages.body_plain:
Dear Carl,

In a standard "four-way cross" of a ABXCD genotype, the coding scheme is NA = missing, 1 = AC, 2 = BC, 3 = AD, 4 = BD, 5 = A = AC or AD, 6 = B = BC or BD, 7 = C = AC or BC, 8 = D = AD or BD, 9 = AC or BD, 10 = AD or BC.
But, for some loci when there are some parental genotype is   AAXBC or ABXCC or ACXBB or ABXBC, we are having some of genotypes that cannot be assigned in this scheme e.g., AA, AB, CC, BB etc. However, when I am importing these data without converting the genotype in number (i.e., 1=AC instead AC= AC or AA=AA)  the R/QTL is accepting this data and reading it in its own way. I am confused how is happening. Can you please explain and give a solution?

Best Regards,
Mehedi

messages.body_plain:
To help keep things straight, I'll refer to the observed marker alleles in lower case, so aa x bc rather than AA x BC.

Now, to your question: You need to have inferred phase, for example, whether a marker is aa x bc, aa x cb, bc x aa or cb x aa.

Then, for a marker like that, there are two possible offspring genotypes: ab or ac. If phase = aa x bc, then ab == AC or BC = C = 7 and ac == AD or BD = D = 8. So for this marker all of the individuals would get codes 7 or 8.

For a marker like ab x bc, you'd have four types of offspring: ab, bb, ac, bc. And ab = AC = 1, bb = BC = 2, ac = AD = 3, and bc = BD = 4.

karl

messages.body_plain:
I would split the marker names into three groups and then use movemarker().

  mnames1 <- markernames(mycross, chr=1)
  n.mark <- length(mnames1)
  mnames1b <- mnames1[seq(2, n.mark, by=3)]
  mnames1c <- mnames1[seq(3, n.mark, by=3)]
  for(marker in mnames1b)
    mycross <- movemarker(mycross, marker, "1b")
  for(marker in mnames1c)
    mycross <- movemarker(mycross, marker, "1c")

karl

Is it possible to assign X-chrpmosome genotype differently from autosome, in this four way cross data set?

Regards,
Mehedi

messages.body_plain:
I think you'll need to use the pattern of genotypes in the offspring to determine whether a marker locus is pseudoautosomal or "normal" X linked. That is, at a given marker, are the males all hemizygous (look like homozygotes, but with the one allele coming from their mother)? I'd call that a "normal" X marker, and would change the male genotype to from say homozygous A to AD, where D would be a placeholder for the Y chromosome.

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] parallel computing
messages.body_plain:
I think what's happening is that each process is pasting the results back on top of mapbt9, so what you get is the result just for whatever chromosome finished last.

I don't have experience with foreach, so I'd use mclapply in the parallel package.  Here's some example code. The key thing is to save the separate results from each chromosome and then paste them back together by just grabbing that chromosome component from thecross$geno. I guess the key thing is to note that mclapply returns a list, each element being the result for a different chromosome.

  # use hyper dataset, selected chromosomes
  data(hyper)
  hyper <- hyper[c(1:3,5:9),]

  library(parallel)

  # do the ordering of markers, one chromosome at a time
  result <- mclapply(chrnames(hyper), orderMarkers, cross=hyper, mc.cores=8)
  names(result) <- chrnames(hyper)

  # combine the results
  hyper.reordered <- hyper
  for(i in chrnames(hyper))
    hyper.reordered$geno[[i]] <- result[[i]]$geno[[i]]

One weakness is that we're passing the full dataset to each process. In the following I create separate cross objects for each chromosome, containing just that chromosome's data:

  hypersub <- vector("list", length(chr))
  names(hypersub) <- chr
  for(i in chr)
    hypersub[[i]] <- hyper[i,]

  # need to make a simple function to pass to lapply
  f <- function(cross, ...) orderMarkers(cross, chr=chrnames(cross)[1], ...)

  # we call mclapply a little differently
  result2 <- mclapply(hypersub, f, mc.cores=8)

  # We combine the results the same way
  hyper.reordered <- hyper
  for(i in chr)
    hyper.reordered$geno[[i]] <- result[[i]]$geno[[i]]

karl

Thanks for your help.

messages.body_plain:
Sorry; the summary function only picks out the single biggest peak on each chromosome. We don't have any facilities, at this point, to do the sort of "bump finding" that would be necessary.

You could do something like this:

  # set up example using hyper data
  data(hyper)
  hyper <- calc.genoprob(hyper)
  out <- scanone(hyper)

  # there's a clear double-bump on chr 1
  plot(out, chr=1)

  # pick out the first peak
  firstpeak <- max(out, chr=1)

  # find second-highest that is at least 20 cM away from first
  secondpeak <- max(out[out$chr==1 & abs(out$pos - firstpeak$pos) > 20,])

I prefer the stepwiseqtl function (e.g., with additive.only=TRUE) to CIM.

karl
